from.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison before the inverse limit: Cocompleteness and tensor-compatible homotopy colimits of dg model localizations.

title: Cocompleteness and tensor-compatible homotopy colimits of dg model localizations
statement:
Use coherent diagrams, mapping spaces, equivalences and limiting or colimiting cocones as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. In particular, coherent diagrams are simplicial maps into quasicategories, transformations are edges of the internal functor simplicial set, and colimiting cocones are initial objects of the coherent comma cocone category, using its right-pinched mapping spaces and weak contractibility. A diagram indexed by an ordinary category $J$ means a diagram on its nerve $N(J)$. Use cochain complexes, quasi-isomorphisms and the derived category convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use locally presentable in the explicit sense of [lem-coef-accessible-monad-presentability]. Fix universes large enough for all categories and small diagram shapes in this statement. Let $\mathcal M$ be a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category, enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups. Suppose there are retract-closed classes $C,F,W$, with $W$ satisfying two-out-of-three, and functorial weak factorization systems $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ generated by sets. A weak factorization system means every map factors as a map of the first class followed by one of the second, and the two classes are exactly each other's diagonal-lifting classes. Assume the enriched model axiom: for $i:A\to B$ in $C$ and $p:X\to Y$ in $F$, the map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,X)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,X)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,Y)}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,Y)$$
is degreewise surjective, and a quasi-isomorphism if $i$ or $p$ belongs to $W$. Let $\mathcal D=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$ be the enriched localization of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal], with derived mapping objects $R\operatorname{Hom}$.

The underlying infinity category of $\mathcal D$ has all small limits and colimits. Its enrichment is tensored over the enhanced derived category $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$: for $K\in\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$ and $X\in\mathcal D$ the derived tensor $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}X$ exists, satisfies the tensor--mapping-object adjunction, and preserves small colimits in each variable. For every small homotopy coherent diagram $A:J\to\mathcal D$ and $Y\in\mathcal D$, its colimit cocone induces an equivalence
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(\operatorname{colim}_J A,Y)\simeq\operatorname{lim}_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(A_j,Y)$$
in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$, natural in $A,Y$. Both sides retain the coherent structure maps; these are homotopy limits and colimits. For $J=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, where $\Delta$ has finite nonempty ordered sets and order-preserving maps, the colimit is the geometric realization and the displayed limit is the derived totalization. Finally $W$ is saturated: an actual morphism of $\mathcal M$ belongs to $W$ if and only if its image in the underlying infinity category of $\mathcal D$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Agent-formulated general dg-model foundation for paragraph 2. WANTED: the derived-enriched tensor and colimit theorem for combinatorial dg model categories. Lurie, Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 1.3.4.22, Propositions 1.3.4.23-24 and Corollary 1.3.4.26 give presentability, homotopy (co)limit comparison and left-Quillen colimit preservation on underlying infinity categories; read online https://people.math.harvard.edu/~lurie/papers/HA.pdf, printed pp. 118-120, not archived. The derived chain-enriched tensor and mapping-object formulation remains an explicit unsplit foundation. Model saturation is the standard model-localization assertion, also mentioned in Harpaz, Lax limits of model categories (2018 version), Remark 10. No Stacks tag states this whole enriched result.

external.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 1.3.4.22, Propositions 1.3.4.23-25 and Corollary 1.3.4.26, printed pp. 118-120. These support only the underlying infinity-categorical assertions; the chain-enriched enhancement remains agent-formulated.

proof.text: First distinguish the two localizations. By [lem-coef-dg-model-underlying-localization], the underlying infinity category $U\mathcal D$ of the enriched localization in the statement is the homotopy coherent localization of the ordinary nerve of $\mathcal M$ at $W$. All hypotheses of that comparison are exactly those assumed here, with the same enriched model axiom and universes. Apply [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability] to this ordinary model structure: $U\mathcal D$ is presentable and has all small colimits. The first assertion of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] supplies all small limits. Put $\mathcal V=\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$; [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] with $R=\mathbf Z$ supplies its presentably symmetric monoidal model, whose tensor is computed on cofibrant complexes.

source.place: Paragraph 2, preliminary identification of the enhancement and underlying presentability; agent-supplied model foundation

proof.text: Write $H(A,B)$ for the ordinary Hom complex of $\mathcal M$. The underlying category is preadditive. If $0$ is an initial object, its identity is its zero endomorphism, so any arrow into it is zero; hence it is also terminal. The tensor and cotensor adjunctions show $H(A,0)=H(0,A)=0$ as complexes: for every complex $K$, maps $K\to H(A,0)$ correspond to the unique map $K\otimes A\to0$, and maps $K\to H(0,A)$ correspond to the unique map $0\to A^K$. Use [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] at $R=\mathbf Z$: complexes have weak equivalences the quasi-isomorphisms, fibrations the degreewise surjections, and cofibrant unit $\mathbf Z[0]$. Thus the given enriched model axiom says exactly that its Hom comparison is a fibration, trivial if either input map is trivial.

source.place: Paragraph 2, zero object and interpretation of the enriched mapping axiom

proof.text:
Let $u:K\to L$ be a cofibration of complexes, $i:A\to B$ a cofibration of $\mathcal M$, and $p:X\to Y$ a fibration of $\mathcal M$. Tensor and enriched Hom adjunctions identify diagonal fillers in a square from
$$(L\otimes A)\amalg_{K\otimes A}(K\otimes B)\longrightarrow L\otimes B$$
to $p$ with fillers in a square from $u$ to $H(B,X)\to H(A,X)\times_{H(A,Y)}H(B,Y)$. The latter Hom map is a trivial fibration if $p$ is trivial, so all such squares lift: the displayed pushout product is a cofibration. If $i$ is trivial, the Hom map is a trivial fibration for every $p$; if $u$ is trivial, it lifts against every fibration of complexes. In either case the pushout product lifts against every $p$ and is a trivial cofibration. Here the lifting characterizations are exactly the given weak factorization systems, and the complex model is [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. Taking $u:0\to K$ or $i:0\to P$ shows that for cofibrant $K,P$, the functors $K\otimes-$ and $-\otimes P$ preserve cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, and $K\otimes P$ is cofibrant.

source.place: Paragraph 2, tensor pushout-product calculation from the given Hom axiom

proof.text: The tensor restricted to cofibrant complexes and cofibrant objects is homotopical separately. To check this without an unquoted Brown lemma, apply [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] to a weak equivalence $f$ between cofibrant inputs: $f=pi$ and $ps=1$, with $p$ a trivial fibration and $i,s$ cofibrations. Two-out-of-three makes $i,s$ trivial cofibrations. Either fixed-cofibrant tensor functor $T$ from step 3 sends $i,s$ to weak equivalences. Since $T(p)T(s)=1$, two-out-of-three makes $T(p)$ one, and hence $T(f)$ one. By [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison], cofibrant inclusions induce enriched localization equivalences, both for $\mathcal M$ and for complexes with the projective monoidal model of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. For the complex model the requisite enriched Hom axiom is the adjoint form of its closed monoidal pushout-product axiom: lifting a generating (trivial) cofibration against the Hom comparison is exactly lifting its pushout product against the given (trivial) fibration. Thus the mapping-comparison theorem applies to complexes as well. Localize the tensor restricted to these cofibrant domains using the multivariable assertion of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] and compose with inverses of those inclusion equivalences. This constructs $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}X$ as an enhanced bifunctor, represented by $QK\otimes QX$. Its coherent associativity and unit maps descend from the ordinary action associativity and $\mathbf Z[0]\otimes P=P$: tensor words in cofibrant inputs remain cofibrant by step 3, and the universal property descends their entire coherence diagrams. No enriched replacement functor is assumed.

source.place: Paragraph 2, construction of the derived scalar tensor on cofibrant domains

proof.text:
For cofibrant complex $K$, cofibrant $P\in\mathcal M$ and fibrant $I\in\mathcal M$, tensoring and cotensoring give the actual enriched adjunctions
$$H(K\otimes P,I)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{Ch}}(K,H(P,I))\cong H(P,I^K).$$
The tensor functors $-\otimes P$ and $K\otimes-$ preserve cofibrations and trivial cofibrations by step 3. Thus [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] applied to their ordinary adjunctions gives left adjoints on underlying coherent localizations in both variables. It also makes $H(P,-)$ and $(-)^K$ right Quillen functors. In particular $I^K$ is fibrant. The same fibrancy assertion follows directly by transposing a lifting square against $I^K\to0$ into a square from its $K$-tensor to $I\to0$. Every complex is fibrant by [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model]. Therefore [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison], including its application to complexes from step 4, identifies all three displayed complexes with the derived mapping objects on these cofibrant/fibrant inputs.

source.place: Paragraph 2, the two actual Quillen adjunctions and their cofibrant/fibrant mapping representatives

proof.text: The derived left functors just obtained agree coherently with the fixed-variable functors constructed in step 4. Indeed apply [lem-coef-fibrant-subcategory-localization] to the opposite of either source model category, taking its fibrations to be the opposite cofibrations. Its pullback hypotheses are pushout stability of cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, and its factorization hypothesis is the (trivial fibration, cofibration) factorization in the opposite model. It gives an equivalence from the ordinary coherent localization of the cofibrant subcategory to that of the full category. By [lem-coef-dg-model-underlying-localization] the latter is the underlying enriched localization. Both candidate left functors restrict to the actual tensor on cofibrant inputs: this is the construction in step 4 and the replacement formula of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. Restriction along the cofibrant inclusion equivalence and along the localization is fully faithful on entire functor categories. Hence the specified restriction comparisons identify the two functors and all their naturality homotopies. Cofibrant representatives cover every fixed scalar and every fixed object.

source.place: Paragraph 2, ordinary cofibrant-localization comparison identifying the two constructions of the left functors

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-dg-quillen-enriched-adjunction-descent] to each enriched Quillen pair in step 5. The source complex model satisfies its hypotheses by [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] and the Hom-axiom check in step 4; the other model is the one assumed in the statement. Its parameter clause and the multivariable assertion of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] retain the actual tensor--Hom isomorphism's naturality in the cofibrant scalar and object and fibrant target. The needed separate homotopicality follows from step 4 and the mapping bifunctor in [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison]. With the tensor identified in step 6, the result is
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}X,Y)\simeq R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal V}(K,R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(X,Y)).$$
Applying $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(\mathbf Z[0],-)$ and the unit adjunction gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{U\mathcal D}(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}X,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(K,R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(X,Y)).$$
Both are coherent equivalences, natural in all three variables.

source.place: Paragraph 2, descent of the enriched tensor--mapping-object comparison with all parameter naturality

proof.text:
Each fixed-variable derived tensor preserves all small coherent colimits. Here is the argument for either left adjoint $F\dashv G$ from steps 5-6. If $c=\operatorname{colim}_J B$ for any small coherent shape $J$, then for every $Y$ the adjunction and the representable colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] give
$$\operatorname{Map}(Fc,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(c,GY)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(B_j,GY)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(FB_j,Y).$$
These equivalences are induced by the image cocone. The same cited criterion therefore makes that image cocone colimiting. This argument applies to arbitrary small simplicial shapes, and does not restrict $J$ to an ordinary category or require rectifying it.

source.place: Paragraph 2, separate small-colimit preservation via the two derived adjunctions

proof.text:
For a coherent small diagram $A:J\to U\mathcal D$ and $Y\in\mathcal D$, put $c=\operatorname{colim}_J A$. Its cocone, followed by contravariant derived Hom, gives the canonical comparison
$$\gamma:R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(c,Y)\longrightarrow\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(A_j,Y)$$
in $\mathcal V$; the limit exists by step 1. For every $K\in\mathcal V$, step 7, step 8, and the two representable (co)limit criteria in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identify $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(K,\gamma)$ with the equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(K,R\operatorname{Hom}(c,Y))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{U\mathcal D}(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}c,Y)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{U\mathcal D}(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}A_j,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(K,\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}R\operatorname{Hom}(A_j,Y)).$$
The Yoneda functor of $\mathcal V$ is fully faithful by that same node, so $\gamma$ is an equivalence. Every map in this chain is induced by the given coherent cocone or the natural tensor adjunction: consequently the equivalence is natural in $A,Y$ and retains the coherent structure maps, including higher homotopies.

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived Hom turns a coherent colimit cocone into a limit cone

proof.text: Take $J=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. The geometric realization of a simplicial object of $U\mathcal D$ means its colimit over this indexing category; derived totalization of the resulting cosimplicial mapping-object diagram means its limit over $\Delta$. Thus step 9 is precisely the asserted realization/totalization equivalence, with the coface and codegeneracy maps that come from the original simplicial object. These are the names for those coherent (co)limits, not a claim about underived totals or ordinary categorical colimits.

source.place: Paragraph 2, definition of realization and derived totalization for the simplicial specialization

proof.text: The zero object from step 2 lets us apply [lem-coef-pointed-model-stability] just for its initial assertion: the ordinary homotopy category of the homotopy coherent localization is the ordinary localization at $W$; no suspension-equivalence or stability conclusion is needed. Via step 1 this is $h(U\mathcal D)$. Apply [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] to the actual ordinary localization $\mathcal M\to h(U\mathcal D)$. It says that an actual map $u$ of $\mathcal M$ belongs to $W$ if and only if its image is an isomorphism there, without cofibrancy or fibrancy hypotheses on its endpoints. An isomorphism in this homotopy category gives an inverse edge with both inverse equations witnessed by homotopies, which is exactly an equivalence edge in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; the reverse implication is immediate. This proves saturation for $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, equivalence detection after the underlying localization comparison
